item.title: Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri: The Runaway-Float Festival — Guide
item.description: The Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri, held each September in the coastal city of Kishiwada, is the most exhilarating and famously reckless festival in Osaka. Teams of hundreds haul danjiri — massive, intricately carved wooden floats weighing several tonnes — through the town not in stately procession but at a flat-out run, the great skill and danger coming at the corners, where the pullers whip the float around a sharp turn without slowing while a leader dances on the roof.

item.title: Saga Summer Gion Festival — Guide
item.description: Like many towns across Japan, Saga celebrates a summer Gion festival, a traditional Shinto festival held to pray for protection from plague and misfortune in the hot months. Rooted in centuries-old custom, Saga’s Gion festivities bring the streets to life with processions of tall, elaborately decorated festival floats, portable shrines (mikoshi) carried by teams of locals, and the beat of drums and chanting, often lit by lanterns as evening falls. The atmosphere is festive and communal, with crowds lining the route, food stalls, summer yukata and a real sense of local pride and tradition.

item.title: Gion Matsuri Guide: Kyoto's Greatest Festival
item.description: Gion Matsuri is the most famous festival in Japan — a spectacular, month-long celebration that takes over Kyoto every July. Centred on Yasaka Shrine and over 1,150 years old, it culminates in the magnificent Yamaboko Junko, grand processions of towering wooden floats — some over 25 metres tall and weighing several tonnes — hauled through the city by teams of men to the music of flutes, drums, and bells. In the evenings before the processions, the Yoiyama street parties fill the downtown with lantern-lit floats, food stalls, and crowds in yukata.
